channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Oil: Hormuz traffic and policy risks – MUFG
item.description: MUFG's Derek Halpenny examines how uncertainty over Strait of Hormuz oil flows and tight US fuel inventories are shaping crude prices.

item.title: Gold eases as traders await clearer signals on the Fed interest rate path
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) remains on the back foot at the start of American trading hours on Thursday after reversing its earlier intraday gains. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,577, after reaching an intraday high of $4,643.

item.title: European Central Bank: September hike prospects strengthen – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Jan von Gerich argues that the European Central Bank remains focused on upside inflation risks and is likely to continue tightening policy.

item.title: Fed’s Schmid warns energy shock is leaking into the economy
item.description: Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid warned on Thursday that inflation remains stubborn and that the energy shock is spreading into the broader economy. With the next meeting approaching, he said the Fed needs more information but remains committed to returning inflation to 2%.

item.title: Fed's Goolsbee warns political interference with Fed could fuel inflation
item.description: Chicago Federal Reserve (Fed) President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday that the economy remains broadly stable but warned that tariffs and war-related price increases are complicating the inflation outlook.

item.title: Euro trims intraday losses as traders weigh Fed-ECB interest rate outlooks
item.description: EUR/USD holds firm on Thursday after coming under pressure on the previous day as the latest US inflation figures helped the US Dollar (USD) regain some lost ground.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed repricing risk weighs on usd – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH Elias Haddad notes the US Dollar (USD) is consolidating gains, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) testing its 200‑day moving average resistance and United States (US) data showing Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index inflation stuck above the Fed’s 2% target

item.title: Swedish Krona: Inflation risks may prompt tougher Riksbank stance - BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu says rising Swedish import prices and continued weakness in the krona are adding to inflation risks. He expects the Riksbank to adopt firmer language on SEK valuations and sees scope for the market to bring forward expectations for the next rate hike.

item.title: Euro: Choppy range trading outlook – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses EUR/USD dynamics around divergent inflation and policy outlooks in the US and Eurozone.

item.title: US Initial Jobless Claims dropped to 203K last week
item.description: According to a report from the US Department of Labor (DOL) released Thursday, the number of US citizens submitting new applications for unemployment insurance fell to 203K for the week ending August 22.

item.title: Brent: Watching support at 84/83 dollars – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts highlight that Brent has pulled back after testing resistance at $95, a level defined by a prior downside gap and a descending trend line from April.

item.title: Canadian Dollar stays vulnerable as US-Canada trade war heats up
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.3870 on Thursday, down a modest 0.05% on the day at the time of writing.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Momentum cools as cross holds above key support
item.description: GBP/JPY trades broadly flat on Thursday after Wednesday’s modest pullback ended a four-day winning streak. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 216.45, with momentum indicators suggesting limited buying interest.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Himino signals hawkish shift - MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes that the Japanese Yen reaction to Deputy Governor Himino’s speech was limited, even as his comments aligned with market expectations for a Bank of Japan rate hike in September.

item.title: ECB Accounts: Another rate hike likely unless inflation outlook improves
item.description: The European Central Bank (ECB) Accounts of the July 22-23 monetary policy meeting show that policymakers remain open to further monetary tightening despite unanimously deciding to keep interest rates unchanged.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA hold view caps near-term upside against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole highlights that the Australian Dollar (AUD) is the only G10 currency gaining this week as hotter July inflation and strong household spending fuel hawkish Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) expectations.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD remains sideways near $68.50, Fed Warsh’s speech awaited
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) trades 0.35% higher to near $68.40 during the European trading session on Thursday, but is broadly sideways in a range between $67.35 and $70 this week.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Kiwi dips below 0.5950 as US Dollar strengthens
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) heads lower for the second consecutive day against a stronger US Dollar (USD) on Monday, as hot US inflation data released on Wednesday has renewed pressure on the US Federal Reserve (Fed) to hike interest rates in the coming months.

item.title: Oil: Hormuz supply recovery eases risk premium – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu at BNY notes that improving flows through the Strait of Hormuz are easing Oil supply fears and supporting a lower Brent price profile. Kuwait and Qatar have restored crude shipments to about 70% of pre-war levels, lifting total Hormuz flows.

item.title: Japanese Yen : Range holds with BoJ hike expectations – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH Elias Haddad notes USD/JPY is stuck between resistance at 160.00 and support at the 200‑day moving average, as Bank of Japan (BoJ) officials maintain hawkish guidance and underlying inflation firms near the 2% target.

item.title: British Pound drops to weekly lows below 1.3600 as US Dollar gathers momentum
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) extends losses for the second consecutive day on Thursday, as the US Dollar (USD) strengthens after the hot US inflation report released on Wednesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains firm on firm RBA interest rate hike prospects
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is up 0.1% at around 0.7180 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Thursday. The Aussie pair remains firm this week due to continued outperformance by the antipodean.

item.title: Euro struggles for direction against British Pound despite upbeat German data
item.description: EUR/GBP trades around 0.8575 on Thursday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day with a modest gain of 0.05%.

item.title: Euro retreats below 1.1650 as inflation data buoys US Dollar ahead of Jackson Hole
item.description: The Euro (EUR) heads lower for the second consecutive day on Thursday, with the US Dollar (USD) supported by strong US inflation data released on Wednesday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Trade war complicates BoC path – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered economist Dan Pan expects the Bank of Canada (BoC) to keep its policy rate at 2.25% and delay a 25bps cut to December, citing a Q2 growth rebound that reduces the need for immediate easing.

item.title: Euro steadies against Japanese Yen as German sentiment beats expectations
item.description: EUR/JPY trades around 185.65 on Thursday at the time of writing, virtually unchanged on the day. The Euro (EUR) benefits from encouraging German data, while the Japanese Yen (JPY) continues to struggle to attract sustained demand amid concerns over Japan’s fiscal position.

item.title: US Dollar: Policy reality supports resilience – OCBC
item.description: OCBC Bank strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong argue that Treasury buybacks are unlikely to trigger sustained Dollar weakness without clear Federal Reserve support to cap yields.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD hits lows sub-$4,600 as US inflation supports the Greenback
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) is giving away the mild recovery seen during Thursday’s Asian session and pulls back below $4,600 during the European morning, as the US Dollar Index (DXY) consolidates above 99.00.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Thursday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $68.39 per troy ounce, up 0.38% from the $68.13 it cost on Wednesday.

item.title: British Pound: Remains under pressure below resistance against Euro – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux and colleagues note that EUR/GBP has rebounded sharply after forming an interim low near 0.8450 in July, but the recovery has stalled around 0.8585.
